# 4 Maccabees Chapter 4 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** Antiochus and the Jerusalem Temple

---

**4:1** Now during the reign of Seleucus Nicanor as king of Asia, Simon — appointed as temple administrator — was in conflict with Onias the high priest about the management of the city marketplace.

**4:2** Unable to prevail over Onias, Simon went to Apollonius son of Thraseas, who was at that time governor of Coele-Syria and Phoenicia.

**4:3** He reported that the Jerusalem treasury was so full of untold wealth that the deposits were beyond counting — and that these funds did not belong to the sacred revenue but were the personal reserve of Ptolemy son of Seleucus, a man of great prominence.

**4:4** Apollonius praised the informer, went to the king, and reported the matter of the rich treasury.

**4:5** Authorized by the king, Apollonius went to Judea with the treacherous Simon and with Menelaus.

**4:6** He declared by royal decree that all the funds were to be transferred to the king's treasury.

**4:7** Onias the high priest, even though well-disposed toward the king, went before his people and told them they must not comply, saying:

**4:8** It is not right for those who have sacred obligations to allow the temple treasury to be given to the royal coffers, for these funds belong to God.

**4:9** Simon, acting with criminal boldness, entered the sanctuary when Onias had gone to the king for consultation, and carried off some of the donations.

**4:10** Then the tyrant Antiochus, informed by the wicked Simon that the treasury was brimming with riches, came up to Jerusalem himself.

**4:11** He declared that if the Jews would not adopt Greek customs, he would put them all to death.

**4:12** When he found that the people as one preferred death to abandoning their ancestral customs, he went to the temple himself to plunder the sacred treasury.

**4:13** Onias, guardian of the sanctuary, called out to God: O Lord, since I have kept faith with your law, protect your holy place now!

**4:14** But Antiochus entered boldly, and his companions came with him to despoil the sacred offerings.

**4:15** But God who watches over all things and punishes the wicked struck Antiochus down.

**4:16** He fell to the ground, suddenly blind, and darkness covered the sanctuary; his companions fled in terror.

**4:17** Yet even then Antiochus in his arrogance pressed on and entered the inner sanctuary.

**4:18** He took the golden altar, the lampstand, the table of showbread, the libation vessels, the censers, the great curtain, and all the temple decorations.

**4:19** He stripped everything and left with great arrogance.

**4:20** He appointed Jason as high priest, a man who was lawless and utterly wicked.

**4:21** Jason offered a bribe of three hundred sixty talents of silver and promised that if given authority he would bring the people into compliance with Greek customs.

**4:22** He was given the high priesthood and immediately began drawing his own people away toward a Greek way of life.

**4:23** He abolished the customs of the ancestral law and introduced customs contrary to the law.

**4:24** He built a gymnasium below the temple citadel and induced the noblest of the young men to wear the Greek broad-brimmed hat.

**4:25** Through the sheer wickedness of the ungodly Jason, Hellenism reached its peak and foreign customs spread everywhere.

**4:26** The priests were no longer interested in their temple duties; they despised the sanctuary, neglected the sacrifices, and hurried to take part in the athletic activities at the wrestling arena.
